utterances.text: Turning then, if I may, to what was formerly part of bundle K8 for that municipality, Mitrovica. I see that on the ELMO at this point. Tell us about that, if you would, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: This is a map of the municipality of Mitrovica, with the major population centre towards the left-hand side of the map and with an annotation on the map with a green star.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Showing a transit location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is there a particular name associated with what you've got as the green star? In other words, do witnesses refer to it as "transit location" or do they call it a -- by the name of a place or what?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: They call it by the name of the village, which is Zabare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see, Zabare Pristina and Donje Zabare?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's just -- now, is there a convergence there of roads or is that a -- that red line, that road goes through that green star, is that a main road or what?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, the hash marks running from top of the map to the bottom, is that a railroad?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, it shows the names of the various small little hamlets and villages that make up the municipality of Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 4, map 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. K62 of Mitrovica. At tab 14 for my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As soon as it's on the ELMO, Witness, you can describe what this is and any significant markings that would be of assistance to the Court.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: This is a town map of Mitrovica. The blue line denotes water courses. The red lines are the major roads through the city. And the course of the railway line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. If I may then turn to the Pristina municipality, map 8, part of what we used to call K7. It is now Exhibit 3, map 8. You created this map, and I take it the routes are in red. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which major -- or is there more than one direction to a border shown on this or only one direction?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: There are two directions shown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: One shows the major highway and railway line from Pristina and Kosovo Polje to the Macedonian border crossing at Djeneral Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's on the bottom right side of the map?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct. The second route is via Stimlje, Suva Reka, Prizren to the Albanian border at Qafe e Morina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Still on that municipality, if we can turn to the bundle K8. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Yes. This map shows the municipality of Pristina with the city of Pristina towards the left-hand side, and just off the map is the town of Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: It's on the left-hand side of the map, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Pristina, that is a major city, I take it, in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Pristina is the principal city in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's a confluence there of roads and railways, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct. The railway is shown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, all the small hamlets are listed, or many of the small hamlets are listed by name on this map?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Madam Clerk.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 4, map 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: K62. I would ask that you look at the town map of Mitrovica, which is found at tab 14. K69, town map of Pristina. I'm sorry, did I say Mitrovica? That was my mistake. Tab 15. This is a slightly larger map, taken because it's a larger city.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, there is a legend on this, showing ten points by name and number; is that correct? And I'm not going to ask you to go through those. Those are depicted on this map?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And otherwise, it's a town map, showing roads and railways, et cetera, and just gives the Court reference points to receive the evidence from the witnesses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'll just move on, if I may. Unless the Court wishes any clarification, I'll just enter it as an exhibit and move on. You've given it a number, Madam Clerk? I've failed to record it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning, then, to the municipality of Djakovica, map -- I think it's map 9 of Exhibit 3, which was formerly K7.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have it on the ELMO. There's blue lines. What does this show?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: This shows routes taken by persons from the city of Djakovica through Prizren to Qafe e Morina, routes taken by displaced persons from the city of Djakovica to Qafe e Prushit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's also another location on the Albanian border?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it also show routes of individuals as to how they got to Djakovica before they went on to those two Albanian border crossings?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those would be the villages to the left, on the map, of Djakovica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Map 9 of Exhibit 3, please. Turning to K8, if I may. That would be -- that's of the Djakovica or Gjakova municipality. Again, that would depend on whether we're talking -- speaking Serbian or Albania; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again this shows that particular municipality and the main city in it?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the various villages and hamlets in that vicinity. Is there also a confluence there of roads? In other words, those black marks and red marks, what are they?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: There is the main road from Pec or Peje through Decani, Djakovica, and then on to Prizren. There are also the number of other roads which lead from Klina and other locations into the city and from the outlying areas, other villages in Djakovica municipality, into the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If I could -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Madam Clerk.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 4, map 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Moving along.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving along, what was formerly K79, Tab 16, the town map of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that's on the ELMO, sir. Again, that's a town map of Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the roads shown and also the site of the MUP building on the right-hand side of the map, near -- two-thirds of the way down; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct. And the VJ barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, where are they located?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're pointing now to about a third of the way down in the centre of the -- of the map?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct. And also in the bottom left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More VJ barracks at the bottom left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else that would be of assistance to the Court to have noted at this point, sir?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: The river crossing here and the Tabak bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And there's an arrow on the bottom corner, pointing to -- is it Prushit, Qafe e Prushit?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Yes. That's the route to Qafe e Prushit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prushit. And what is that? Is that an Albanian border town?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's one of the Albania border crossings. The main road here goes to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by "here," just for the record, you're pointing to the red line leading to the right of the map, off the map?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Past the MUP site.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: And to follow that line to the top left-hand corner of the map is the road which takes you to Decani and Peje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. And I think that's already been assigned a number by Madam Clerk.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, the next exhibit, which I don't propose to show to the witness, is one that was known as K560.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I understand that you are aware that this is a videotape of approximately an hour and a half long. Do you know what's on this videotape? Can you tell us what it relates to?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: The footage on that videotape shows damage to a number of residential premises in Djakovica. It shows damage to a large part of the marketplace in the Hudum [phoen] area of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: It further shows, towards the end, shots in the cemetery at Djakovica, concluding with footage of graffiti painted on walls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has part of that video been shown during a portion of my opening?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, copies of this video have been disclosed both to the accused and to the amici, and we propose, unless the Court orders otherwise, that that be marked as an exhibit at this point, without the necessity of playing it at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Let it be marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: If I may move to the next municipality, sir, Gnjilane. Part of K7 is the map. Again, red lines -- I guess these are all different colour reds, are they? They just don't --

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct. They don't print differently, and certainly on the ELMO they tend to look similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. But in the aggregate, you can make the distinction between the various routes, or the nuances in colour shades?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. All right. Now, this is a little bit more complicated. Perhaps you can tell us what these lines show.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: These lines depict routes taken by displaced persons from various sites in the Gnjilane municipality, travelling both west, or to the left, to Urosevac, to the border at Djeneral Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's the border of Macedonia, is it?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct. To a secondary border crossing at Globocica, with Macedonia. They also depict routes travelling to the right, or east, into the Presevo valley, and then south to the Macedonian border. Additionally, they show routes taken through the mountainous areas, into Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Part of K8 was the municipality map. Again the legend, again the names of the villages, and again showing the roads converging in Gnjilane; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Might that be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 4, map 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to paragraph 13, Urosevac. Referring now to part of K7. And perhaps you could simply describe what this map depicts.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: This map depicts routes taken from a number of villages and from the town of Urosevac. The villages centre on Urosevac and then south to the border crossing with Macedonia at Djeneral Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I see that there's a railroad line going from Urosevac to Djeneral Jankovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct. The main highway between Skopje in Macedonia and Pristina runs through the town of Urosevac and both the railway and the road feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the villages are to the east of Urosevac, going to Urosevac, and then straight, in sort of a southerly direction, to the bottom of the map, to Djeneral Jankovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: That was map -- sorry. Map 11, I believe, Madam Clerk. And the town map of Urosevac, please, formerly tab 17. There's no K8 for this site.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once it's on the ELMO, just tell us what it is, please, and point out any sites that may be of assistance to the Court to accept the witnesses' evidence at a later time.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: It is a town map of Ferizaj, or Urosevac. It shows the main highway, with Lipljan and Pristina at the top, Kacanik and the border crossing at Djeneral Jankovic on the right-hand side. It shows the railway line travelling through the town, with an indication as to the location of the railway station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving, then, if I may, to the municipality of Kacanik, I only have one map to show you in this matter, and that would be formerly part of K7, map 12. That's now on the ELMO. There's a number of sort of purple-blue lines here that look like they're going to need some description.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: These are routes taken by displaced persons through the border crossing at Globocica, Djeneral Jankovic --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Globocica, just for the record, that is a border crossing with what country or state or province?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: With Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Macedonia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: It also shows routes taken across the mountainous area to the east of Djeneral Jankovic, and it also describes the routes taken by persons who remained displaced within this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so that I'm clear again: Djeneral Jankovic, that's also Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving, then, if I may, to Decani, two maps here, part of K7 and part of K8. First of all, let's go to map 13 of what was formerly K7, now Exhibit 3. So it's map 13. You have that on there?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does this show?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: This shows the routes from a number of centres around Decani and then the path taken by the displaced persons through Djakovica, Prizren, to the border at Qafe e Morina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, that's on the border with Albania; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is through Decani, through Djakovica, Prizren, and then to the border?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. K8 of that municipality, of that -- is there anything of particular significance you feel you should address the Court's attention to at this point on this map?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: The municipal area of Decani is in the centre. Above that on the page is the municipal area of Pec, or Peje. On the bottom right-hand corner of this map is the municipal area of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the community we just saw in the previous map?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Correct. It shows the -- many of the smaller hamlets and villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Finally, Vucitrn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Number for that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 4, map 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Map 14 of what I propose is Exhibit 3, this is the Vucitrn map. Do you have that on there? And this is in green.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that show?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: It shows the movement of displaced persons from the town of Vucitrn and a number of villages into an area to the east or to the north-east of the city, and then various routes, one of which goes through Pristina, Lipljan, Stimlje, Suva Reka, Prizren, to the border at Qafe e Morina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there appear to be arrows going to the north as well. What is that?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct. It's a route which was taken from Vushtrri, through Mitrovica, Leposavic to the town of Novi Pazar in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say Vushtrri, that's Vucitrn?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And part of K8 for that municipality, there's a map. What can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: It shows the municipality of Vushtrri, or Vucitrn, with the town being shown in the centre. To the top right -- sorry, to the top left is the city of Mitrovica. The main road between Mitrovica and Pristina is shown, along with the railway line between Mitrovica and Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Number, Madam Clerk?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 4, map 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. And Your Honours, again, a video, what was formerly marked as K131.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're familiar with that videotape, are you, Mr. Spargo?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And very briefly, can you tell the Court what is contained on that particular video?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That videotape shows footage of a large number of displaced persons moving through the villages in the Studime e Eperme area. It then shows a number of deceased persons and other incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so that the Court is clear, the source -- in other words, this is not taken by journalists or -- or do you know who the source of this video would be, most of the footage?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: The footage on this was taken by one of the local inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's taken by a local inhabitant of Kosovo, sort of like a home video that was then turned over to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I see. Again, Your Honours, we propose to enter that as an exhibit without playing it. Again, all copies have been disclosed to all parties, including the accused. Again, Mr. Kay and I have indicated that we're not relying on any sound. I don't think that one comes with sound, but we're not asking that any sound on any of these videotapes be part of the evidence, simply the video images.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in the summary, Your Honours, I want to skip all of paragraph 17 and take us to the very last paragraph, 18, which talks about the proposed entry of three videos, videos marked in our exhibit list as K1, K2, and K3. Again, the proposal is that these be tendered much as I have the last two videos, and perhaps if we can deal with the first video, K1, Mr. Spargo can tell the Court briefly what it contains.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Video number K1 is a BBC compilation video of various news broadcasts. It shows displaced persons crossing the border at various times early in the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "at times early in the conflict," do I understand that is between the 26th of March and the 30th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: If there is no objection, might that be marked as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Video referred to on our exhibit list as K2, sir. You're familiar with the footage on that video?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us a very brief description of what we can expect to find on that? First of all, is it a BBC news tape?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: All these three exhibits are press footage from the BBC via stories that were broadcast on the news service. This exhibit further shows displaced persons arriving at border crossings. Included in this is footage of persons walking along a railway line. There is footage also of persons on railway trains. There is additional footage of displaced persons in the camps in Macedonia and Albania.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Unless there's any objection, I think we're up to 15, Madam -- 15, Madam Clerk?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This was marked Prosecution Exhibit 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, Witness, the third videotape, K3 formerly in our exhibit list. What, if anything, does that depict, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: This again is a compilation of news broadcasts. It shows the city of Pristina. It shows displaced persons crossing the border and at refugee points. It shows one of the few pieces of footage taken inside Kosovo during the displacement of the Kosovo Albanians. It continues with additional footage of the arrival of KFOR in the city of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything on that video about damage sustained by NATO airstrikes?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: The opening segment is a news broadcast taken in Pristina, showing damage to the post office building and other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Unless there's any objection, that would then become Exhibit 16, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And those are all the questions I propose to ask of this witness at this time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We shall have to see these videos in due course and view them out of court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It might be helpful to know how long they are, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Well, yes. Perhaps the witness can be of assistance with that. I've indicated that the first video, I believe, was an hour and a half, and I failed to note the amount of time on K1, 2, or 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is it recorded on the video itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. There is, actually, Your Honours -- we can supply a precis in the binders, I believe, under tabs 1 -- tabs 2, 3 and 4, which I have here. Tab 2, for example, tells us exactly what is in there and gives us counter readings but not -- I can't find on this document under tab 2 the length of the video, just counter readings and then a very brief description of what it contains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Where would we find that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall I help the Court, as I viewed them last night? It's three hours 20 minutes, about --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: For all three aggregate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, for all the videos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: We can -- we do have these references with counter reading numbers, unless my learned friend objects that those be supplied to the Court so they could find the relevant passages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That might be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Here is a reference for K1. Should I provide copies to the Court and to my learned friends after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, during the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: During the adjournment. Thank you very much. Those are all my questions of Mr. Spargo. Perhaps my learned friends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, have you any questions of this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You explained at the beginning that the routes that you drew in refer to individual people, the people that you questioned. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How -- according to -- in your assessment, in your assessment, how many Albanian refugees passed out through those routes, left through those routes?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Based on the figures that were provided by the UNHCR, the greater percentage of persons displaced travelled through the border crossings at Rozaje into Montenegro, into Albania at Qafe e Prushit and Qafe e Morina, and the Macedonian border crossings at Globocica and Djeneral Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many would you say? What number?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: The number is documented by the UNHCR and numbers some 800.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Eight hundred thousand, you say. You said that this occurred in the period from after the 26th of March onwards, from the 26th of March onwards. Is that correct? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: The deportation or the movement of people commenced in large numbers as of the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They began on the 26th of March. How long did they go on for, these movements of people?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Until a day or two before the entry of NATO under the Military Technical Agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that all this movement was between the 26th of March and the end of the bombing; is that correct? You situate it between those -- in that period?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: They are the limits, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, we have taken note of the fact that all the refugees fled during the bombing. Do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. This witness has purely produced a plan. That is all he's done, brought a series of maps. He cannot answer any questions as how -- to how the refugees came to move or anything of that sort. As I understand it, that's the issue that we're going to have to decide. Now, all he's done is produce a map, having read a series of statements. So can you confine your questions to those matters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you please, the witness himself quoted dates, and the witness himself stated dates a moment ago. Let me move on to my next question. As he followed the movement of refugees, as he has testified here, from the area of Kosovo and Metohija, my question is:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see how many Serb refugees left Kosovo at that time?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That wasn't within the mandate of the inquiry I was conducting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know the UNHCR figures? You mentioned another figure by the UNHCR and that was that 100.000 Serbs left Kosovo during that same period. Are you aware of that fact? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: What is this based on?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On facts and figures put out by the relevant organs, those who followed refugees and information about refugees and their movements. Now, I'm asking you whether you are aware of that fact, of that figure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Spargo, if you don't know, just say you don't know. No doubt we'll hear some other evidence about it, rather than having an argument with the witness -- or with the accused, rather. You don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not aware of the figures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the following, the number of Serb and Albanian -- how many Serb and Albanian inhabitants there are in Kosovo? What is the figure?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That was always imprecise, following the boycott of the Kosovo Albanians in the 1991 census. I'm not aware of the exact breakdown or total numbers of the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, at least roughly, the proportion between the Albanian and Serb population, the ratio, approximately?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: My understanding was that the estimate was that the Kosovo Albanians consisted of around 90 per cent of the population, with the remainder being made up of both Serbian and other ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are we going to hear a witness, Mr. Ryneveld, who is going to deal with population? This witness hasn't so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour. We do intend to call reports and witnesses to deal with precisely that issue. Dr. Patrick Ball's report and Ms. Blayo, these are demographers who will be calling evidence of that nature. That's not within the ambit of this witness's evidence, nor had I intended to lead that in chief, and I understand that cross-examination is normally limited to the led area in chief. However, if the witness is able to answer, I'm not objecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You may not be, but it's a question of time. Mr. Milosevic, you can ask questions about the population to the witnesses who are going to deal with it, who are experts in the field and who will give evidence about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know the answers to those questions. I just relied, in posing my questions, on the statement made by the witness, who said here a moment ago that it was not his job to ascertain how many Serb refugees left Kosovo. So that is why I wanted to hear from him whether he knew the proportion, the ratio, the population ratio. And if he says that 800.000 people left and, according to official facts and figures, 100.000 Serb refugees left, then proportionately more Serbs left Kosovo because of the bombing than was the case with the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will hear -- Mr. Milosevic, we'll hear argument about it. We'll hear it all in due course. Now, can we move on to the next point relevant to this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that's all I'm doing. I'm dealing with points relevant to the testimony of this witness and nothing more than that. This testimony -- by this testimony, undoubtedly the Prosecution, when speaking of the movement of refugees and only the movement of one ethnic group, who are doubtlessly fleeing from the bombing, are being maliciously qualified as deportation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the question? We don't want comments. You can make them in due course. What is the question for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have seen that mention is being made continuously and reference made to refugees, what is being referred to is refugees, and including displaced persons within the frameworks of inside Kosovo, the territory inside Kosovo. We have also seen a great deal of maps in which the witness has stated in the affirmative the names of the towns, what they're called, where the roads are, where the railway lines are, where the rivers are, questions of that type. Now, as the indictment -- as the Prosecution has brought this witness to speak about deportation, I should like to ask the witness the following:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anywhere on these maps, the maps that we have seen, was there a collection centre, a camp, a concentration centre for deportation of any kind? I have not seen it on any of the maps that you showed us. Now, I'm asking you, did it exist or did it not? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: There were concentration points, and the witnesses who will give either live evidence or through 92 bis will describe those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you whether there was a concentration camp of any kind.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Is this a concentration camp in the form of what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you don't know, say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand the term he's using.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A point of concentration when somebody is travelling can be a railway station, for example. It can be a bus station too. It can also be a main road. And you have described to us those elements on the map. But what I'm talking about is any kind of -- the existence of any kind of organised place of concentration that was under guard, that was guarded, that was walled in, or anything of that kind. And as you have not included it in any of your maps, does that mean that it did not exist or did you fail to include it in your maps intentionally? So all I'm asking you is: Did it exist or did it not; yes or no.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: There were points, which the witnesses will address, as to concentration areas. Due to the type of map we were looking to achieve, something simple to assist the Court in the direction people moved, we did not include this type of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's suggested to you that you intentionally left information off the map. Would that be true or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir. It was never the intention to put this type of information on the map. The witnesses we're relying on, they can describe exactly where these places were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you are making up your lack of material facts by witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness simply said he drew a map. Now, what is the question that arises from that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From that, it emerges that on the witness's maps there is nothing except roads, railways, rivers, and towns. You could have taken those maps ten years ago and you would see the same roads, railways, rivers, and towns on them. And when people are fleeing from a bombing, they move along roads and railway lines. They use the communication routes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Unless you've got any more questions, we're going to let this witness go.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do have some more questions. I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you worked as a policeman.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you ensure the presence of individuals whom you questioned, interviewed?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: It was either by arresting them at the time, when they were found to be committing offences, or by invitation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I heard the first part of your sentence, but not the second. What did you say in the second part?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: By invitation, by requesting them to attend at a police station for questioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you select the individuals you invited to come to the police station for statement taking and questioning?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours. As a matter of clarification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is no relevance in this, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: No, but also a point of clarification. Is he talking about in his former life as a policeman in Australia, or now, or -- I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I wouldn't worry for the moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is my question clear? I am asking how he ensured the presence of the individuals whom he questioned in Kosovo and Metohija and on the basis of whose statements he established this. I'm talking about those individuals, those persons. I'm not talking about how he ensured the presence of persons in his previous career. And I think I put it very clearly, so that your comment is completely unfounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Just a moment, Mr. Milosevic. Let the witness answer. Did you interview any of these witnesses yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of what was all -- were all these documents devised? You talked to the witnesses. You have brought in a witness who did not talk to the individuals upon whose statements he drew these maps, on the basis of whose statements the product of everything he set forward was made.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Investigators from the ICTY went out, spoke to witnesses and other persons, obtained statements from them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Spargo. Registrar, this is Exhibit 3 and map 1. Could you show that on the ELMO. This is just an example. You noticed there are some comments on the right bottom side. There are the source, and there's names up here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court what these names are.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Berisha, Elshani, Hoti, and Salihi. They are the witnesses who were selected which told the best accounts of the different events and will be either giving live evidence or via 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Have you interviewed them yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You just saw statements of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you made the map on the basis of their statements.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, the witness claims that he drew up the maps on the basis of the statements made by the staff of the Prosecution; yes or no.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: The statements were taken by the staff of the Prosecution from the Office of the Prosecutor. The testimony within those statements, as you will hear, will be the testimony of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know who was present when the statements were taken from the witnesses that you mention?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: I would need to refer to each of those statements to see who the investigating person from the OTP was and who the interpreters were at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Spargo, as Judge May has told you, if you don't know, just say, "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't recall each individual case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It therefore emerges that you just drew up the maps in conformity with instructions given you by the staff and clerks of the Prosecution; yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Based on the witness testimonies, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Nothing arising. Thank you, Your Honour. Questioned by the Court

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Spargo, did you say that all these maps are prepared, produced by you alone?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note some bundle of -- Exhibit 4, some town maps. There's a note: Analyst Alex Nereuta.

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Nereuta Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Nereuta. Who is he?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: He is one of the other analysts on the team I work for. He, in fact, did the -- perhaps we didn't make it clear. He did the municipality maps and the town maps, which are the other exhibits. The ones which show the routes taken by the displaced persons, they were the ones that I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the Corel Draw is some other separate programme other than ArcView you had used?

utterances.speaker: STEPHEN SPARGO
utterances.text: Corel Draw is another programme which was found to be best for taking those maps from the HCIC, the other UN agency, and making them fit to pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Spargo. Thank you for coming to give evidence. You're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That would be a convenient moment to adjourn. Half past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before my learned friend Ms. Romano takes the next witness, and indeed she and Mr. Ryneveld will be taking most of the crime-base witnesses, can I just revert to the 92 bis position? The history of service of materials includes this: That although the process of serving binders on the Chamber was arrested, for various reasons, it was completed in respect of the amici and in respect of the accused, so that for deportations, and indeed for killing sites, he's been provided with binders that contained 92 bis -- or proposed 92 bis witness statements. He may not have taken the opportunity to read them, but he's been provided with them, probably two or three times, but latterly specifically in relation to the issue of deportations, which is now coming up. My concern, as I explained this morning, was to ensure that, when we come to consider whether these statements may properly be adduced under the provisions of 92 bis, there shouldn't be any technical shortcoming arising from his not having read them or claiming that he hasn't had an opportunity to read them and therefore not being in a position to cross-examine in light of what they contain. And I don't know if the Chamber has had an opportunity to give any further thought to this or to give any thought to what routines we should adopt to ensure that he's best protected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We've in fact had a paper from the amicus on the subject which we would need to consider.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think we can really deal with any of the Rule 92 bis statements this week. Effectively, it seems to me the sensible course is to review the position at the beginning of next week or at a convenient moment next week in the evidence. There are matters of principle involved here, and it's important, of course, that we give them full consideration. In some ways, this may be the first time that the Tribunal has considered the use of Rule 92 bis, at least in an extensive way, and it would be helpful to have a full discussion, and, if possible, to lay down some guidelines for the rest of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. We look forward to addressing the Court on that next week. Can I ask that it be not on Monday, for various reasons? I shall not be here on Monday, but I shall be here as from Tuesday again. And I believe there are a number of other administrative matters that have got to be dealt with, in particular with relation to the Bosnian Croatian parts of the indictment. So maybe there will be a convenient time that we can fix to deal with all these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: At some time next week. Yes. Call the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: The Prosecution call Agim Zeqiri.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Stand up to take the declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Examined by Ms. Romano

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zeqiri, can you please state your full name for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Agim Zeqiri.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you were born.

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: On the 9th of June, 1952.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you born?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: In Celina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's your profession, Mr. Zeqiri?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: I'm a farmer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any military experience or training?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zeqiri, have you always lived in the village of Celina?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, always in Celina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where Celina is located?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Celina is situated between Rahovec, Prizren and Gjakova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close is Celina to the village of Prizren?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: 17 kilometres from the city of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far is the village of Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Gjakova is 16 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there other villages near Celina?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: And there is Orahovac, which is 10 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zeqiri, are you a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many Muslims lived in your village before the war?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: There was about 7.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all of them were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Almost all of them, and there were five households who were Romany, gypsies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you, Mr. Zeqiri, to focus on the period before the NATO bombing, and 1998 until March 1999, and I will ask you some questions. Before March 1999, do you remember seeing the army in your village?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: The Serbian army, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any army.

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Well, the Serb army was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were they present?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: They were stationed on the main road, the main asphalt road, from early March 1998. They came and they were there two hours in the morning and two hours in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that they were there two hours in the morning and in the afternoon, what do you mean? Were they in Celina?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No. They were down on the main road. They were doing exercises in the direction of Gjakova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see them from Celina?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes; army people with uniforms, tanks, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to me what colour is the uniform?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Like the colour of grass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What equipment did they have?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: They had ammunition, they had machine-guns; they had everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any vehicles?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes. They had tanks. There were armed vehicles, jeeps, armoured personnel carriers, pinzgauer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prior March, 1999, prior to the NATO bombing, did you see police in your village?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, they came from time to time to check up, make checks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of checks?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: They were looking for arms, for weapons. They were checking up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it usual for the police to come to Celina?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Well, they came. They used to come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they used to do when they came to Celina?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: They would go into people's houses and they would say, "Bring us your weapons." And if people had them or not, they would force them to go down to the police station in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened in the police station?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Their main objective was to get money out of you, and we had to find, come up with money and bring the money to them, and then there was no problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it happen to you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No, not to me. No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it happened to other people from your village?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zeqiri, did you ever see roadblocks in Celina?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes, there were. From the beginning of 1999, there were checks to get into the town of Gjakova and Prizren and to get into Orahovac. In all the towns, there were military centres, bases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did they have these roadblocks?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Because of us. How should I tell you? If we wanted to go into town, we couldn't -- you know, if we had anything, we couldn't dare go into town, because they would control you, they would check up on you, or even old people they would check up on. They would mistreat you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was checking up?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe them?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: They had like white gloves, and they would do the checking up. They would do the controls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the NATO bombing, also around 1998 and before March 1999, did you see members of the KLA in your village?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Well, from time to time. There weren't really any. They would cross through the town on the road from time to time. Rarely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you or were you a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: I was a village councillor and I did some -- I helped them with some minor services. That's about all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by that time also, did you remember seeing any fighting between the KLA members and the VJ or the police?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the day when the NATO bombing started?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: It was on the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: I was at home with my family. We heard about the bombings in the evening on the 24th, but we were at home all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was with you in your home?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: We were about 18 family members together, all together there at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your close family, how many members were there?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: You mean the whole family?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Just your close family.

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: There are 26 of us altogether. I'm the 27th, actually -- or the 7th. Sorry, the 7th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your wife with you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, she was with me. We spent the whole night all together, all of us. There were the children there. We were with the children. The family of my uncle and my own family, all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen in your village that night?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No, nothing happened that night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your reaction to the NATO bombing?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: What can I say for a reaction? We weren't really -- maybe we were satisfied because, well, the Serbs said that they were going to attack us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Zeqiri, on the next day after the NATO bombing, were you at home?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: On the next day, the 25th of March, the army arrived up at the end of the village. They were stationed up there. They came maybe for five or ten minutes, and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at home?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see -- when you say that the army arrived at the village, from where did you see that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: We were in the courtyard of our house. I was with my uncle in the courtyard, and we could see it from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far were they from your house?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: They were up at the end, one of the village, we were at the other end. Maybe a kilometre. About a kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they do anything? Did they fire shells?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They started burning down a whole neighbourhood. There were infantry -- there were troops there, there was a school up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Zeqiri, when you say they're infantry troops, did the army come to your village, come to Celina?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, in the afternoon. They surrounded the village entirely, around 3.00 in the afternoon. They surrounded the whole village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, you were at home?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: I had gone out with my family and with a gypsy family, eight people, who are neighbours of ours, right beside us. We went out about 20 metres away, down to a stream, with my uncle and all the gypsy family all together. We went out to the stream.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you leave your house? Wasn't it safe?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No. We weren't safe at the stream either, but we thought, if they came down to us, the infantry, the troops, they would come down along the main road and would burn all the houses and would maybe continue in that direction. That's the reason we went out towards the stream.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zeqiri, when you say "they came," can you describe the uniform?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes. I saw uniforms, army uniforms and police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw both, army and police?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you and your family were at the stream, what happened after?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: One of the villagers said to us that we should -- all the men, we should leave the women and go up 20 metres farther away so that we would be separated from the women and children. So we went up. We could see the bombing from -- as far as we could tell what was going on, but we could see it from up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many men went with you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: We were about seven or eight men altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were hiding in that place, could you see the police or the army?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No, we couldn't see them from there, no. We went away because we were afraid they would get into the houses and would go onto the roof and shoot at us. We were down in a ravine. The family was hiding down in a ravine. That's why they were down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody go back to check on the women and children?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes. My uncle went down. Yes. Yes, I did. Some of us had gone to a house in the periphery, and I told my uncle, "Go and see what the women and children are doing, and then I will come back to join you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to your uncle?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: The son of my uncle, Bajram, he too went down. I have never seen them ever since. Some others left. I was left alone with the gypsy man. He left me -- he went some five metres away to see if the other group went to the house in the periphery. I told him, "Don't go, because they will kill you." This is the words we exchanged together, and then we heard fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said -- what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: We heard the fire, the shots, and I saw that a bullet hit the gypsy. He came up to me, just turned his body in my direction. Then they fired him at him again and he fell down in a ditch. And then I left and hid until 12.00, in a stream down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far were you from this man that was shot?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: With my uncle, you mean? No, with the gypsy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the gypsy.

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Some five metres, five or six metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who shot him?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: I saw him just falling down before my very eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you see who was shooting?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No, I did not. I couldn't see that. Only I saw him falling, as I said, down in front of my eyes, but I didn't see who shot him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your uncle that went back to see the children and the women, have you seen him again?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No. I did not see him or my family or his family. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zeqiri, where did you spend the night of the 25th?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: The night -- I spent the night of 25th of March, as I was telling you, in a stream, with two or three, in fact, friends of mine. They were in Slaniste, in a little bit higher place. We were in a lower place. And they were firing just in vain. I heard fire shots all the time. Then after midnight, the firing stopped and I told my friends, "Let's go away from here." And then we climbed the mountain and went up to a meadow on top. I wanted to go to see some cousins of mine. I hadn't seen them for 20 years. I wanted to visit them. And they saw me when I climbed the hill, and they started to fire, but then I ran. I went to a place where I stayed until two other friends of mine came and joined me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a place where you spent the night?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes. After midnight, I went to my cousin's, as I said. It was about 5.00, and I joined them. Then together with them, with a family - two families, actually - I went with them and stayed together until 5.00 in the afternoon. We found a hiding place in a mountain called Pisjak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you arrive in this place Pisjak? Were you alone? There were more people there?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes. There were over 5.000 or 6.000 people, people from five or six villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is Pisjak located?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: It is located, let's say, some three kilometres outside the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened while you were there? First of all, I want to draw your attention to the 28th of March. You were still in Pisjak at that time?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No. On the 27th I was there. As I told you, on the 26th, I joined my cousins. On the 27th, I was in Pisjak. On the 28th, at 10.00, we were surrounded from all sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Surrounded by whom?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: The army troops and the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they wearing the same uniform that you described before?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't lead the witness -- just a moment. Just a moment, please. Ms. Romano, don't lead the witness on these rather crucial issues, please. Perhaps -- you can ask him what uniforms they were in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes. They had put on army and police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The army, what colour of uniform, do you remember, they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Some green uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any insignia?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of insignia? Can you describe?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: You mean the police insignia? No. The army, no. Only the police. The day they surrounded us, they were black in their faces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will get to the police. And what colour uniform of the police?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: They had the gloves on. They had a white band on their arms and some red insignia also on the arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what was written in the band in the arm?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes: "Police." I could read "police."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zeqiri, what happened after the police surrounded you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: They surrounded us, and then a villager took some clothes, white clothes, and waved it, and we surrendered. We called the people, telling them, "We have surrendered."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they do after you did that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: After the people came there, we walked for some 20 metres, and they separated the women from the men, the women and the children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "they," you are referring to whom?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: The army and the police, both of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the Court that they separated men, women, and children. Can you describe how they did that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: We men were told by someone who had painted his face black, he told us, "Lie down on the ground." And we had to do that, to lie on our stomachs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say they had their face black, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: The army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were -- it was masks or they were painted? When you say --

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No. They had painted their faces black. It was not a mask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any weapons with them?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, of course they had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of weapons?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Guns. Automatic guns, munitions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zeqiri, after they separated you from the women, what happened?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: First, as I told you, they told us first to lie down. Then a young man, they took him away and we heard the fire shots. They killed him. And then we stayed there, lying on the ground. Then that man that I told you with his black face, he came there. When he came up to me, he stopped there for two minutes, let's say, and they started to kick me on my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who kicked you? Who kicked you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: That man that I told you with the black face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he kick you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: With his -- he kicked me on the back of my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he do after?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Then he said, "Get up," and then he tied our hands. "Put your hands behind your waist."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: We continued to keep our hands behind our backs, and then a friend of his appeared before us. He did not have anything -- he had a normal face. And then we continued to stand up. And in Serbian, he said -- this was the words he said -- that means, "Shall we take them to Belgrade or to Albania?" That is the translation of the Serbian word he mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Just a second. I don't ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything else?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No, he did not. We continued to walk with our hands behind our head. They were behind us. When we came to the village, all the people were there, and we saw the village all in smoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zeqiri, I'm going to interrupt you just for a moment. Coming back to Pisjak, where you were with the police or the army person, can you describe when they beat you, they continued beating you? What did they do to you before they started saying if they're going to Albania or not?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No, they did not beat us any more. Only that friend of ours, they shot dead, and me myself, they kicked. I didn't see anyone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did they kick you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: On my head. They kicked me, with his boots on my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you still suffering from this -- from the beatings that you received at that time?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, I have problems. I will tell you later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Zeqiri. So after that ended, after they finished with this, did they send -- where did they send the men and the women?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: We were walking, as I said, down to the village, and then when we arrived in the village, we saw the houses burning and we saw police and army troops coming from various streets of the village after they had set fire to the houses. And then when we went to the asphalt road, they checked, they searched in our pockets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they say, while you were walking -- all the time that you were walking, the police and the army were guiding you. At that time, did they say anything to you, to other villagers?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, they were there all the time on our side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were saying anything to you or to the other villagers?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: No. They searched, as I said. We asked the men before we arrived at the asphalt road, and then they told us to raise our hands up and raise three fingers. The police were there on both our sides. We were walking on the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were they guiding you to?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: To Albania.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But before arriving to Albania, you mentioned a village that you stopped at. Where was this village?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: The village in Krusa Mala, at the station. There were two policemen at the bridge, and we saw the police with automatic guns and they put us in a ditch up to our waist. And we had to go there, to obey their orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zeqiri, they were guiding you from the hill -- down from the hill down to the asphalt and then from the asphalt to this village, Krusa Mala. During this time, the police and army were next to you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Yes, they were with us. They escorted us all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many people were with you at that time?

utterances.speaker: AGIM ZEQIRI
utterances.text: Our first group was composed of about 4.000 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
